item.description:

The Prime Minister of Iraq announces a reduction in the autonomy of the Kurds in Iraq regarding oil and border crossings – the Kurds are furious

Ali al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, issued an official statement last night in which he declared that from now on, the Iraqi government will impose its sovereignty also in the areas of Kurdish autonomy in northern Iraq.

Al-Zaidi announced that border crossings, oil exports, and the management of oil fields in the northern regions of Iraq will be directly controlled by the government.
He declared the dismissal of the relevant officials in these areas.

Oil and border crossings are the cornerstones of the Kurds' power in Iraq. Depriving them leaves the Kurds exposed.

The background to this move is claims by the Iraqi government regarding the illegal smuggling of oil from Iraq’s resources, as well as unlawful movement at the border crossings.

The move is somewhat reminiscent of the takeover by Syrian President Abu Mohammad al-Julani of Kurdish assets in Syria, accompanied by the deafening silence of the Trump administration in the face of the move.

Ali al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, is fully supported by Trump, who assisted in his election to the position.

Some speculate on social networks that this is Trump’s revenge on the Kurds over the issue of weapons supplied to them for the war against the Iranian regime—which “disappeared.”

For those interested – the full remarks made by the judges presiding over Netanyahu’s trial to the Attorney General:

“…It should be clarified that this does not constitute an expression of no confidence in the prosecution representatives appearing before us.

The Attorney General’s appearance is required because the decision to file the indictment was made by the Attorney General, who also signed it, although a different Attorney General held office at the time; and because, ultimately, it is the Attorney General – the current officeholder – who decides how the proceedings will continue.

Our starting point is that, following the conclusion of Mr. Netanyahu’s testimony, the proceedings have reached a juncture at which, in our opinion, it is appropriate to examine how to proceed. In our view, the public interest requires reconsideration.

We emphasize that these remarks reflect our impressions thus far; we have not written a verdict. We wish to reflect our understanding of the matters before us and share our thoughts and insights.

These remarks relate solely to Mr. Netanyahu, as we have not yet heard the other defendants.

The primary focus is the first charge. It appears to us that the bribery charge presents considerable difficulties.

First, the quid pro quo element rests primarily on the allegation that Mr. Netanyahu gave instructions to Mr. Filber. This allegation is based mainly on Filber’s testimony. On its face, it is difficult to establish factual findings on the basis of this testimony, both in light of the course of the investigation and the changes in his account, and in light of objective evidence that is inconsistent with it.

Furthermore, there is serious doubt as to whether the allegation of exceptional responsiveness has been proven. It is unclear against what benchmark this responsiveness is alleged to have been exceptional. There is serious doubt as to whether the evidentiary foundation substantiates the allegation.

There is also serious doubt as to whether it has been proven that Mr. Netanyahu was aware, in real time, of the alleged exceptional responsiveness.

In view of these doubts, the alleged conflict of interest involving Mr. Netanyahu also presents difficulties, including with regard to the offense of breach of trust.

Regarding this charge, we assess the likelihood of conviction to be sufficiently low to justify reconsidering the matter.

As for the second charge, we have serious doubts as to whether the conduct described in the indictment constitutes a criminal offense.

The alleged offense concerns the fact that Mr. Netanyahu did not discontinue his discussions with Mr. Mozes; engaged in detailed discussions with him regarding the components of the proposal; and took actions aimed at presenting a genuine possibility that he would use his governmental authority and senior public office to advance legislation benefiting Mr. Mozes. It is alleged that such conduct by someone holding the highest position in the executive branch profoundly and fundamentally undermines the rule of law, integrity in public office, and public trust.

In our opinion, there is a significant question as to whether these legal and normative conclusions indeed follow from the factual description in the indictment, and whether they are supported by the evidence presented before us.

Nevertheless, since the state has not been given an opportunity to present structured legal arguments on this matter, we believe that, should the state wish to do so, it would be appropriate for us to hear such arguments before deciding how to proceed. We assume that such arguments would also address the allegation in the indictment concerning the use of the powers of public office to obtain a personal benefit. Here, too, it is not apparent that the conduct described in the indictment and the evidence presented substantiate this allegation.

We believe that we have reached a juncture at which these matters need to be clarified and refined. > >

הודעה משותפת לדובר צה"ל ודוברות שב"כ:

יממה לאחר שחוסל מפקדו: צה"ל ושב"כ חיסלו את ראש מנגנון ביטחון הפנים של צפון רצועת עזה בארגון הטרור חמאס

צה״ל ושב״כ תקפו בצפון רצועת עזה וחיסלו הלילה (ד׳), את המחבל מחמד אבו אלעוף, ששימש כראש מנגנון ביטחון הפנים של צפון רצועת עזה בארגון הטרור חמאס.

אבו אלעוף היה דמות משמעותית בארגון הטרור והיווה מוקד ידע שעסק בניסיונות הגבלת חופש הפעולה המבצעי של צה״ל ברצועה.
חיסולו מהווה פגיעה ביכולות הניהול של המנגנון ומתווסף לחיסול של מפקדו - נעים מחמד עאשור אבו נחל, ראש מנגנון ביטחון הפנים, שבוצע אתמול.

כמו כן, חיסולו מתווסף גם לפעילות של צה"ל ושב"כ במהלך חודש ספטמבר האחרון, במסגרתה כוחות מיוחדים של שב"כ פשטו על מבנה במרחב העיר עזה ועצרו את ראש ביטחון הפנים של ארגון הטרור חמאס בכלל רצועת עזה.

מנגנון ביטחון הפנים של ארגון הטרור חמאס משמש את ארגון הטרור, בין היתר, לשימור שלטונו ברצועת עזה תוך פגיעה באוכלוסיה המקומית.
לאורך תקופת המלחמה, המנגנון היה אחראי על הוצאה להורג של מתנגדי ארגון הטרור והפעלת מתקני עינויים על מנת לדכא את מחאות המתנגדים נגד שלטון הטרור של חמאס.
